hypotheses.construction_plan: Take the master function F(z)=log Gamma(z). Apply D=d/dz once to F to obtain polygamma(0,z), and apply D twice to F to obtain polygamma(1,z). The raw expression is then D F + D^2 F without further simplification.
required_assumptions: Gamma(z) is nonzero and log Gamma(z) is sufficiently differentiable
polygamma(0,z) is defined as d/dz log Gamma(z)
polygamma(1,z) is defined as d^2/dz^2 log Gamma(z)
hypotheses.rationale: Both terms are consecutive derivative orders of the same logarithmic Gamma master function, so the sum is structurally a differential operator applied to one latent object.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Start from the two-parameter family P(n,z)=polygamma(n,z). The two terms are obtained by specializing n=0 and n=1 respectively, and the raw expression is P(0,z)+P(1,z).
required_assumptions: polygamma(n,z) is defined for the nonnegative integer orders n=0 and n=1
hypotheses.rationale: The two summands are adjacent members of the standard polygamma order family, so they share a common order-parameterized template.
